newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians, Israeli troops clash in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians, Israeli troops clash in West Bank.

text.p: Hundreds of Palestinians stoned Israeli soldiers in the West Bank towns of Bethlehem and Hebron on Tuesday during protests against Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, witnesses said.
They said Israeli soldiers fired teargas and rubber bullets at about 200 stone-throwers who attacked troops guarding the tomb of the biblical matriarch Rachel at the northern entrance to Bethlehem.
Some demonstrators wore gas masks during the clashes.
Witnesses said more than 10 Palestinians were taken by ambulance to a hospital in the nearby Beit Jalla hospital for treatment from teargas inhalation or rubber-bullet injuries.
About 200 youths pelted Israeli soldiers in a part of Hebron that is still under occupation, witnesses said. They said the soldiers refrained from firing at the demonstrators.
An Israeli army spokeswoman confirmed the clashes in Bethlehem and said the army was using teargas to quell them.
Israel's groundbreaking on 6,500 housing units for Jews on the outskirts of Arab East Jerusalem last week angered Palestinians, sparking almost daily demonstrations in several areas in the West Bank.
President Yasser Arafat's Fatah movement called on Palestinians to confront Jewish settlement activity with non-violent protests and by blocking roads used by Jewish settlers in the West Bank.
